# Permissions and security

An agent runs commands as you, with your files and credentials.  Two controls limit it: a
*sandbox* restricts what it can touch, and *approvals* decide when it must ask first.

## Sandboxing

- A sandbox is an operating-system restriction on file writes and network access.  It applies to every command the agent runs, including scripts it wrote.
- Codex sandboxes by default: writes are limited to the project folder and the network is off.  In Claude Code, `/sandbox` turns it on.
- Both halves matter.  Without network limits, an agent can send out your SSH keys.  Without file limits, it can change things outside the project.

## Approval modes

| | Claude Code | Codex |
|---|---|---|
| Read only | `plan` mode | `--sandbox read-only` |
| Default | `auto`: acts, with a background safety check | `workspace-write` sandbox, asks to leave it |
| No checks | `--dangerously-skip-permissions` | `--yolo` |

- Allowlist commands you approve repeatedly (`/permissions` in Claude Code).  After many prompts in a row you stop reading them.
- A boundary stated in chat ("don't push") can be lost when the session compacts.  For a guarantee, use a deny rule or a [hook](04-extending.qmd#hooks).
- Use the no-checks modes only inside a container or VM that holds no credentials.  A July 2026 Codex bug [could delete the home directory](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Jul/16/bad-codex-bug/) in that mode.
- Commit before starting a task.  Git is the undo button.

## Prompt injection

- Anything the agent reads can contain instructions: web pages, issues, files from other people, MCP tool output.  The agent may follow them.
- The risk grows with each permission.  An agent with no network access cannot send data anywhere.
- Keep credentials out of reach.  Don't paste API keys into the chat, and don't run agents in a shell with production credentials loaded.

## Unattended runs

- An unattended agent cannot ask for approval, so its permissions are the only limit.  Grant the minimum: `codex exec` is read-only by default; `claude -p` takes `--allowedTools`.
- In CI, the repository's own configuration is input.  `claude -p` runs a repository's hooks and MCP servers without a trust prompt unless you pass `--bare`.
- Pass API keys to the single command that needs them, not to the whole job.
- Have the agent open a pull request.  Do not let it merge or deploy.
